acceptance_tests_proposed: Exact roundtrip of the actual208-unit navigation with original HTML hashes unchanged and all pages/indexes bounded
Oversize child_ids but small text; oversize text; oversize unknown metadata; empty text; Unicode and escaped JSON strings
Equation spans/continuation boundaries and table heading/link order retained; no whitespace loss
Missing/reordered/duplicated/mutated fragment rejected; original source/nav tamper rejected
Native independent review/adjud policy, full candidate/asset review and original source access unchanged
claims_not_made: Mathematical equivalence proof of existing extraction
v5 cost reduction before old comparator and independent gate
Production implementation or historical artifact modification

container_overlap.recommendation: Do NOT drop nested units in current protocol. Root-only still retains shared words but removes explicit unit identities and equation/theorem navigation. Optional reference-based exact reassembly would require a separate schema and tests; modest ~14.69% navigation-byte reduction does not establish model savings.

math_representation.boundary: Raw source remains authoritative. Alttext-vs-rendered mathematical equivalence was not semantically proven here. Do not simplify TeX, strip symbols, replace formulas with prose, or claim raw HTML byte difference is new achievable savings.
math_representation.existing_behavior: EvidenceHTMLParser already inserts alttext once per active selected container and suppresses nested MathML glyphs and TeX annotations. Remaining repeated equations largely come from overlapping selected containers, not accidental inclusion of both MathML and alttext in the same leaf.

measured_structure.first_failure: S5.T2 at unit57; not solely the longest17,492-byte text. Child-ID arrays and pretty-JSON overhead matter.
measured_structure.largest_text_description: A5.T5 is a table of model abbreviations and Physiome links, not a giant equation.

minimal_new_protocol_proposal: Keep original HTML, original source_navigation bytes, all existing scientific/public review obligations. Implement as separate opt-in version only after approval.

Retain existing complete-unit pages when they fit. Only oversize units get an explicitly fragmented representation: stable unit index/id/hash, original full unit metadata, ordered child_ids fragments and ordered text fragments with exact character ranges.
Compute serialized frame bytes, not only text bytes. Page both text and child_ids (and any future oversized field via explicit exact fallback); otherwise A4.T4 still fails.

Split text on safe UTF8/codepoint boundaries without stripping, normalizing or summarizing. Prefer whitespace boundaries outside intact TeX alttext spans; this source max alttext246 bytes makes intact-formula splitting feasible. If an indivisible equation itself exceeds bound, mark continuation explicitly and require all fragments plus source verification; never claim fragments individually carry complete meaning.

Verify joining ordered text fragments and child_id lists exactly reconstructs the original unit, then reconstruct every original navigation unit and compare canonical digest and original input hashes. Reject gaps, duplicates, stale hashes, reordered fragments, extra files, links, and incomplete indexes.
Index must advertise fragment count/completeness and every source locator. Page large indexes as well. A partial fragment read is not a complete unit read or scientific acceptance.

Use conservative serialized page bound such as12KB with small line counts; tool line-number rendering is additional bytes and token limits remain tool-specific. Never assert 12KB guarantees a token ceiling on every native interface.

No root-only semantic dedup or new math transform in the minimal repair. Avoiding all-source fallback is worth a small isolated change; reduction in model tokens/time remains an empirical question for a future authorized trial.

read_failure.interpretation: Single partial HTML Read exceeded tool limit; not an observed aggregate multi-Read batch limit. Dense HTML line ranges do not bound tokens. No inference of full read completion after later smaller reads.
